links.comparator_used: Junior and senior radiologists reading independently without AI (also compared with the AI system alone)
links.outcome: Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, AUC) of junior radiologists for benign vs malignant thyroid nodules on ultrasound
links.effect: Against the 2e criteria, junior radiologists' specificity rose from 0.837 to 0.921, accuracy from 0.833 to 0.895 and AUC from 0.829 to 0.871 (all p<0.001), with sensitivity unchanged at 0.820. Against pathology, accuracy rose from 0.745 to 0.798 (p=0.014) and AUC from 0.744 to 0.798 (p=0.012). Against the arbitration committee, AUC rose from 0.878 to 0.909 (p=0.006). AI-assisted juniors matched senior radiologists against pathology (all p>0.05). Senior radiologists showed no significant change with AI.
links.tradeoff: AI misled junior radiologists in 31 nodules (17 benign and 14 malignant that were originally correct), versus 193 corrected. Sensitivity did not improve. Against the arbitration committee standard, AI-assisted juniors still did not reach senior level (all p<0.05). AI and senior radiologists failed together on 140 nodules. The AI gave only binary outputs with no probability shown.
links.quote: Furthermore, AI assistance significantly improved the performance of junior radiologists in the diagnosis of thyroid nodules, and their diagnostic performance was comparable to that of senior radiologists when pathological results were taken as the gold standard (all p > 0.05).

design_hint: AI assistance for junior radiologists (human-in-the-loop review)
